articles.q: What’s on the main screen?
a: Speed is at the top, tiles with ride data are below it, and widgets such as the map, weather or heart rate are at the bottom.

figure.alt: Main screen: speed at the top, tiles below, widgets at the bottom.

articles.q: How do I see more tiles and widgets?
a: Swipe the tiles or widgets sideways to go to the next page.

figure.alt: A finger swipes the tiles sideways to show the next page.

articles.q: How do I resize parts of the screen?
a: Drag the handle below the speed or above the widgets.

figure.alt: Dragging the handle below the speed resizes the areas.

articles.q: How do I change the speed gauge or a tile?
a: Hold the speed to choose a gauge. Hold a tile to change the data it shows.

figure.alt: Holding the speed changes the gauge: bar, arc, ring, dial.

articles.q: Where do I change the look of the app?
a: In the menu you can choose the style, light or dark theme, speed gauge and screen brightness.

figure.alt: Menu, the Appearance section, then style, theme and gauge.

articles.q: How do I record a ride?
a: ● starts recording and ‖ pauses it.

figure.alt: The ● button starts recording, the ‖ button pauses it.

articles.q: How do I finish recording?
a: While paused, press ■ and choose Save or Delete. An empty ride is not saved.

figure.alt: While paused, the ■ button offers Save or Delete.

articles.q: What does auto-pause do?
a: It pauses recording when you stop and resumes when you ride on. Turn it on with the switch in the menu.

figure.alt: Speed chart: recording pauses while stopped and resumes when moving.

articles.q: How does the ride list work?
a: Tap a month name to collapse or expand it. The month summary is below the name.

figure.alt: Tapping a month name collapses and expands its rides.

articles.q: How do I delete a ride?
a: Swipe a ride left. Hold a ride to select several and delete them together.

figure.alt: Swiping a ride to the left reveals Delete.

articles.q: What do ride details show?
a: The map, summary and charts. Drag along a chart to see that spot on the map. Drag the data sheet to shrink or enlarge the map.

figure.alt: Dragging along the chart shows the same spot on the map.

articles.q: How do I colour the track on the map?
a: In ride details, the button on the map colours the track by speed or gradient. In Premium, also by heart rate zones.

figure.alt: The track on the map coloured by speed, gradient and heart rate zones.

articles.q: What does full analysis include?
a: A power chart, time in zones, best efforts, calories and the weather during your ride. The data is also saved in the free edition, so after purchase the analysis covers older rides too.

figure.alt: Heart rate bars in zone colours and the time spent in each zone.

articles.q: How do I export a ride?
a: In the ride menu, choose Share GPX. The file contains full data, including sensors. FIT export is available in Premium.

figure.alt: Ride, the ⋮ menu, Share GPX.

articles.q: How do I import a GPX file?
a: Open a GPX file in Rydee, for example from a file manager. You can add it as a ride and, in Premium, navigate along that route.

figure.alt: GPX file, open in Rydee, add a ride.

articles.q: What is the Climbs list?
a: The climbs you have ridden, with records and all your rides of each one. There is also a climbs section in ride details.

figure.alt: A list of climbs with profile, length, gradient and record.

articles.q: How do I choose widgets?
a: On the Widgets screen, choose which ones to show and in what order. At the bottom of a widget you can switch the data range.

figure.alt: Menu, the Widgets screen, choice and order.

articles.q: What does the Terrain widget show?
a: Speed and cadence over elevation, gradient, and climbs and descents.

figure.alt: Speed and cadence over elevation, plus the gradient.

articles.q: What does the Heart rate widget show?
a: History plus current, average and maximum heart rate. In Premium also zones, time in zones and drift. Requires a heart rate monitor.

figure.alt: Heart rate history in zone colours and time in zones.

articles.q: How does the Laps widget work?
a: It works while recording and counts laps by distance: every 1, 2, 3, 5 or 10 km or miles. It shows the difference to the previous lap, plus your best, average and slowest.

figure.alt: Laps every 2 km with time and difference to the previous one.

articles.q: What does the Power widget show?
a: 3, 10 and 30 second power, W/kg, NP, IF, TSS, work in kJ and zones. Requires a power meter.

figure.alt: Power in the colours of 7 zones and time in zones.

articles.q: What does the Climb widget show?
a: The detected climb, VAM and the profile behind you. While navigating or on a known climb, also the profile ahead, and on a known climb the difference to your record.

figure.alt: Climb profile behind and ahead of you, VAM and the difference to your record.

articles.q: How does the Music widget work?
a: It shows what’s playing in another app, such as Spotify. Title and cover appear after you grant notification access. Tap the app name to pick another player.
Playback and volume controls are available in Premium.

articles.q: How do I use the map?
a: Pan and zoom with two fingers or the + and − buttons. The button in the top right corner switches between north up and heading up.

figure.alt: The + button zooms in, the compass switches between north up and heading up.

articles.q: How do I start navigation?
a: The navigation button on the map opens destination choice: search, a point on the map (hold) or favorites.

figure.alt: Map, the navigation button, choosing a destination.

articles.q: What does the guidance bar show?
a: The next turn and your arrival time. A sound warns before a turn and when you leave the route.

figure.alt: The guidance bar counts down to the turn and warns with a sound.

articles.q: What do the wind colours mean?
a: The weather widget shows wind relative to your direction: red for headwind, green for tailwind, grey for crosswind. In the free edition, the arrow shows wind relative to north.
articles.keywords: wind weather forecast met norway color

figure.alt: Wind relative to your direction: red headwind, green tailwind, grey crosswind.

articles.q: How do I add a sensor?
a: Open Sensors in the menu. Heart rate monitors, cadence sensors, power meters and bike radars are supported. Power meters and radar require Premium.
articles.keywords: bluetooth ble heart rate cadence pairing

figure.alt: Menu, Sensors, picking a sensor.

articles.q: How does the radar work?
a: Vehicles from the radar appear on the bar at the right edge of the screen. A sound warns of a new vehicle.

figure.alt: A bar at the right edge of the screen with approaching vehicles.

articles.q: How do I connect Strava?
a: Open Integrations in the menu and connect your Strava account. You can upload rides and see starred segments.

figure.alt: Menu, Integrations, Strava, Connect.

articles.q: How do I save rides to Health Connect?
a: In Integrations, connect Health Connect and choose the permissions. You can turn on automatic saving or save a ride from its menu. Rydee only writes data and reads nothing from Health Connect.

figure.alt: Menu, Integrations, Health Connect, permissions.

articles.q: What’s different in Premium?
a: You can get Premium as a subscription or as a one-time purchase. Both unlock the same features, including navigation, power meters, radar, climbs, zones, full analysis and all styles.

figure.alt: Free and Premium editions, Premium as a subscription or one-time purchase.

articles.q: How do I cancel my subscription?
a: You manage your subscription in your Google Play or App Store account settings. When it ends, the app returns to the Free edition. Your rides and saved settings stay, and everything comes back if you renew Premium.

figure.alt: Store, Subscriptions, Rydee, Cancel.

articles.q: Do I need an account?
a: No. Rydee works without an account. Your rides and settings are on your phone and in its backup, if you have it turned on.

figure.alt: Rides stay on the phone and in its backup, with no Rydee account.

articles.q: How do I delete my data?
a: Delete rides from the list or uninstall the app. Data you previously sent to Strava or Health Connect is deleted in those services.

figure.alt: Data is on the phone and in its backup, not on a Rydee server.
